title: data.pdf — section 23
text:
(1) Where an accused’s solicitor purports to give on behalf of the accused—
(a) a defence statement under section 5, 6 or 6B, or
(b) a statement of the kind mentioned in section 6B(4),
the statement shall, unless the contrary is proved, be deemed to be given with the
authority of the accused.

(2) If it appears to the judge at a pre-trial hearing that an accused has failed to comply
fully with section 5, 6B or 6C, so that there is a possibility of comment being made or
inferences drawn under section 11(5), he shall warn the accused accordingly.

(3) In subsection (2) “pre-trial hearing” has the same meaning as in Part 4 (see section 39).

(4) The judge in a trial before a judge and jury—
(a) may direct that the jury be given a copy of any defence statement, and
(b) if he does so, may direct that it be edited so as not to include references to
matters evidence of which would be inadmissible.
